card.name: Scattered points in contraindication and threshold text
card.fires_on: Punctuation or word endings just before a list item or restriction, mostly in contraindication and renal-impairment sentences. Examples are the comma after an eGFR unit, the % after a minimum mark, and 'not' in 'should not be administered'.

modes.label: Closing a renal threshold
modes.description: A closing parenthesis or comma right after an eGFR value and unit in a contraindication.
modes.example: contraindicated in patients with severe renal impairment (an eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m 2<< ),>> end stage-renal disease (ESRD

modes.label: Inside a restriction or warning phrase
modes.description: A word within a 'should not' or injury or perforation phrase in label warnings.
modes.example: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS Divalproex sodium extended-release tablets should<< not>> be administered to patients with hepatic disease

modes.label: Requirement wording in general text
modes.description: A word or symbol in a must-meet requirement, or in an emphatic sentence about change.
modes.example: for students to complete each assessment item satisfactorily: To complete each of the assessment items satisfactorily, students must obtain at least 50<<%>> of the marks available for each assessment item

card.writes: It seems to push toward Chinese words for must, basic principle and strictly forbidden, which suggests rule or requirement wording.
card.plain: It fires at spots in rule-like sentences, such as kidney cutoffs and 'should not' restrictions, where a requirement is being stated.
